Dear Resident(s):

Georgia law requires that we notify tenants regarding the disposition of their security deposit after they move out.
Our Records indicate that you paid a deposit of $350.00 for pet (SD insurance for regular security deposit) on the property
you leased from Excalibur.

Your current balance due is more than your Security Deposit amount. We have, therefore, applied the deposit to
outstanding charges. The remaining balance is still due as shown on the attached ledger.

 If you moved out prior to the end of your lease without the Landlord's consent then you owe rent through the end of the
 lease or until a new tenant moves in and starts paying rent. If this is your circumstance then the charges on the attached
 register show rent charged through the end of the lease. Once the property has been re-rented and we know the date that
 the new tenant starts paying rent, your charges for rent will be reduced accordingly.

 Please send in certified funds for payment in full or call to arrange a payment schedule within 30 days of the date of this
 letter. If we have not heard from you within 30 days the unpaid balance may be sent to a collection agency. This might
 have a negative impact on your credit rating.

Please contact our office as soon as possible so that we may resolve this situation.

Sincerely,

Taliyah King
For Excalibur Homes, LLC
tking@excaliburhomes.com

  On Wed, Aug 7, 2024 at 9:48 PM Ciera Mouncil <cieracairo757@yahoo.com> wrote:
  Michele,

  I am writing to formally dispute the charges that have been added to my final balance following
  my move-out from the property at 2517 Shropshire Place, where I was a tenant from March
  2021. Throughout my tenancy, I consistently paid for Rhino Insurance as required.

  Upon reviewing the itemized charges, I believe that many of the issues cited fall under normal
  wear and tear, which is to be expected after living in a home for three years. According to
  Georgia law, normal wear and tear cannot be charged to tenants. This includes, but is not limited
  to, the following:

  Broken Blinds and Bulbs: These items naturally deteriorate over time and are the landlord's
  responsibility to replace as part of regular maintenance. During my tenancy, there were no
  routine inspections or maintenance visits to replace or repair these items.

  Carpet Condition: Carpet wear is typical after three years of occupancy. There were no efforts
  made by the management to clean or maintain the carpets during my stay, which would have
  helped prevent excessive wear.

  Lawn Service: The responsibility for lawn maintenance after move-out should not fall on me as a
  former tenant. The lease agreement did not stipulate that lawn care would be my responsibility
  once I vacated the property.

  However, I am willing to forego my security deposit I kindly request that you review these charges
  and adjust my final balance accordingly. Please provide me with an updated statement at your
  earliest convenience. Should you have any questions or require further clarification, feel free to
  contact me.

  Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to resolving this dispute promptly and
  amicably.

  Sincerely,

  Ciera Mouncil

  Good afternoon,

https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/?ik=8877b7e174&view=pt&search=all&permmsgid=msg-f:1808105616292977843&simpl=msg-f:1808105616292977843  1/3
9/11/24, 4:20 PM  PURE Property Management Mail - Fwd: 2517 Shropshire - Move out
  Please see the attached Move Out Inspection, Photos, Move In Inspection and Security Deposit
  Transmittal.

  Please note the following:
  1. I consulted your move in inspection report and you are not being charged for any pre-existing
  damages that are noted on the form
  2. Normal wear & tear is best defined at what does not cost the owner any extra to cure for a typical
  turn around for the next resident. For example, if there is extra wall work needed due to the minor
  holes and such and if the painter charges extra for that service (sanding, additional patching,
  sanding and then sealing) then the owner is only responsible for the cost of the final coat of paint.
  Also, if the carpet has dirt or stains that will come out with the normal cleaning process, then there
  will be no charge to the resident except for any additional charges from the service due to the
  extraordinary dirt or stains.
  3. The lease requires you to maintain good housekeeping at all times and to return the house to us
  completely clean. If not, whatever the cost is to complete the cleaning of only those items or areas
  that are not clean will be chargeable.
  4. The lease further requires you to maintain the lawn (mow grass, trim shrubs, weed beds, rake
  leaves, etc.) as well as keep the yard clear and free of rubbish.
  5. If you left trash at the end of the street or in the driveway, then we will charge you to remove the
  trash you left.
  6. Just because it is listed upon the Move Out Inspection form or there is a photo of an area or item,
  does not mean that there is any additional cost due from you to cure. It just means it is different
  from the move in or it is for the owner to see so it can be cured for the next resident.
  7. The attached Security Deposit Transmittal is based upon the estimated or actual cost to cure the
  damages listed or complete the move out maintenance required in your lease. If the actual cost to
  cure is less or more, then the SDT will be adjusted accordingly prior to the end of the 30-day period
  allowed by state law to finalize your deposit.

  Any and all disputes you wish to make regarding the damages/lack of maintenance found must be in
  writing and sent by e-mail.
